summary: A GeoPackage, or a ZIP whose card names a shapefile set, is no longer refused in a batch. Publishing its
card queues one fenced job, intake-native-derivative. The geo service reads the original from object
storage onto scratch disk (hash and size checked), reads each layer in windows of 1,000 features (keyset
by row id for a GeoPackage, record position for a shapefile) and streams one GeoJSON FeatureCollection
per layer plus a hashed locator sidecar. Each derivative is kept as its own large-original-v1 child
through the receipt /uploads uses, named by its lineage, and enrolled like a dropped file, so the large
GeoJSON path reads it unchanged (D3; largeStateKey needed no change). The CB1 small direct import is

D1: Geometry and attributes are written as decoded: no reprojection, rounding, renamed or added
attributes; Z is kept. The stated CRS is written as crs:{type:'name',properties:{name:'EPSG:n'}}.
A GeoPackage row or shapefile record that cannot be decoded (bad header, measure values, a CRS
other than the layer's, a binary, non-finite or unsafe-integer attribute) is not written; the
sidecar lists it with its position and reason.
D1_deviation_no_crs: A layer with no stated CRS is not written at all, rather than written with none. The large reader
reads a FeatureCollection without a crs member as RFC 7946 EPSG:4326, so a derivative without one
would be a guessed system. Instead the original's item rests at needs_answer, its words naming
the layer: 'Not converted until its coordinate reference system is stated: <layer> (states no
coordinate reference system)'. Stated layers of the same file are still kept and enrolled.
D2: Each child keeps inspection.nativeDerivative: version native-derivative/1, conversion
native_gis_to_geojson@1, readerVersion native-gis-window/1, original source id, revision, SHA-256
and item id, format, layer, ordinal, CRS, features, notWritten and the sidecar's key, bytes and
SHA-256. The sidecar (JSON lines) starts with a header naming the conversion, reader, original
hash, layer and position kind (row id field, or .dbf member and record sequence), then one line
per source row in order: {feature:n, position:p} or {feature:null, position:p, reason}.
decisions.D3: A two-layer GeoPackage gives two children; each takes the large GeoJSON path unchanged.
decisions.D4: No stop was needed: the large path took the derivative with no change to intake-large.ts.

docs/api/source-pins.json repinned; docs/api/openapi.json and the api-client types regenerated, no change.
tests/intake-ledger.test.ts: the fixture records each job's operation; a shapefile ZIP expects its conversion job.
limits: Each child's lineage is merged after its receipt finalises, in its own transaction (as ZL1 does); a
crash between them leaves a child without lineage that a rerun does not find and keeps again.
Derivative and sidecar objects stay under native-derivatives/<original sha>/ in object storage.
A shapefile layer with Z or M values is not converted (named in the original's words).
An original over 128 MiB, or a derivative that would pass 128 MiB, is refused by the converter, so the
original rests not understood (NATIVE_DERIVATIVE_FILE); the large reader's own ceiling is the same.
The conversion is one synchronous call to the geo service bounded at the large reader's read time;
the job renews its lease every minute meanwhile.
The proof stops at kept, enrolled children whose bytes the large reader reads in parts; the walk to a
package (layout approval, mapping, officer confirmation) on a running stack was not run here.
